title: Police Wanted to Search Your Entire Phone — Legally? #Shorts
description:
Police pull you over for expired tags — and after you're arrested, a detective wants to scroll through everything on your phone. With no warrant.

Your photos, your messages, your location history — more private than a search of your entire house, all sitting in your pocket. After David Riley was arrested, a detective searched his phone and used what was on it to tie him to a shooting.

In 2014, the Supreme Court said no — unanimously. A phone is not just another pocket. Searching it needs a warrant. This is general history, not legal advice.

Watch the full story on the channel.

#Shorts #FourthAmendment #Privacy #KnowYourRights #SupremeCourt #Documentary
